section_summary: This section contains police and prosecutorial accounts of the May 1949 Tokyo labor demonstrations, a survey of Japanese attitudes toward foreign countries, and reports on labor, communism, and party politics. It also includes accounts of Hokkaido opinion, commercial developments, and the beginning of an article on Soviet policy and the possibility of revolution in Japan.

subfiles.title: MPD Daily Report: Meeting at Tokyo Metropolitan Office
subfiles.from: Chief, Guard and Traffic Division, Metropolitan Police Department
subfiles.about: Reports the May 31 protest against the Public Safety Ordinance Bill and the police response.
subfiles.summary: About 10,000 workers attended a meeting that developed into an unauthorized demonstration around the Metropolitan Assembly Hall. Police ordered dispersal, deployed reserves, arrested 66 people, and reported 66 slightly injured officers. The report also notes an aborted student rally near the Imperial Palace.

subfiles.title: Incident at the Tokyo Metropolitan Office: Death of Kinji Hashimoto
subfiles.about: Summarizes the investigation into Kinji Hashimoto's death during the May 30 demonstration.
subfiles.summary: Investigators found no sufficient evidence that Hashimoto fell from a building or was deliberately struck. They inferred that he fell amid a crowd and was trampled, concluding that no identifiable criminal act caused his death.

subfiles.title: Japanese Opinion Poll concerning Basic Attitudes toward Foreign Countries
subfiles.from: U.S. chargé d'affaires ad interim, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits a survey report on Japanese preferences among foreign countries.
subfiles.summary: Reports that America was most liked and Russia most disliked in a nationwide poll.

subfiles.title: Basic Attitudes Toward Foreign Countries
subfiles.from: Civil Information and Education Section, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Analyzes Japanese responses to questions about the most liked and disliked foreign countries.
subfiles.summary: A weighted sample of 8,011 adults placed America first among liked countries at 62 percent and Russia first among disliked countries at 53 percent. The report examines correlations by country, age, sex, occupation, and residence, while warning that occupation conditions may have influenced answers. An appendix explains sampling and weighting; the final page lists other surveys in the series.

subfiles.title: Threats Against the Lives of General MacArthur and Prime Minister Yoshida
subfiles.from: Cloyce K. Huston, chargé d'affaires ad interim
subfiles.about: Reports security precautions and threats directed at Yoshida and MacArthur.
subfiles.summary: Says MacArthur requested blood samples for Yoshida; MacArthur reportedly abandoned his own escort despite threats.

subfiles.title: Recent Developments in the Democratization League
subfiles.about: Transmits Jane M. Alden's memorandum on the anti-communist labor movement.
subfiles.summary: Describes the Democratization League's growth within unions and its close but uneasy ties to the Socialist Party. Its leaders aim to turn that party into a labor party without surrendering union autonomy.

subfiles.title: Recent Developments in the Democratization League
subfiles.about: Studies Mindo's union organizing and its relationship with the Socialist Party.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum traces Mindo's strategy of winning control of local and national unions before withdrawing them from communist-led federations. It details membership and leadership in Osaka, differing views about Socialist Party affiliation, and the emerging National Council of Labor Unions. Alden anticipates conflict among Mindo, Sodomei, and party factions over leadership of a non-communist labor movement.

subfiles.title: Leaders of the Osaka Region Democratization League of Labor Unions
subfiles.about: Lists officers and executive committee members of the Osaka regional league.
subfiles.summary: Names regional leaders and their union affiliations; several names are illegible in the OCR.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 451
subfiles.about: Summarizes a report on communist tactics amid railway layoffs and violent incidents.
subfiles.summary: Notes alleged Communist organization of local violence and growing Japanese revulsion after Shimoyama's death.

subfiles.title: Telegram on Shimoyama's Death
subfiles.about: Relays a Soviet press account of Japanese accusations concerning Shimoyama's death.
subfiles.summary: Reports a Pravda claim that the murder accusation was provocative and that Shimoyama died by suicide.

subfiles.title: Factions in the Democratic Liberal Party
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits a memorandum and roster on Democratic Liberal Party factions.
subfiles.summary: Sebald emphasizes Yoshida's strengthening position and the decline of older party bosses, while raising concern about succession if Yoshida leaves leadership.

subfiles.title: Factions in the Democratic Liberal Party
subfiles.about: Analyzes shifts among Democratic Liberal Party factions and Yoshida's negotiations with Democrats.
subfiles.summary: Alden describes Yoshida's expanding faction and the weakening of Ono, Yamazaki, Shidehara, Shukuto, and neutral groups. She discusses the lack of an obvious successor and Yoshida's efforts to absorb the Inukai and Ashida Democratic factions.

subfiles.title: Factional Affiliations of Diet Members of Democratic Liberal Party
subfiles.about: Lists Diet members by Democratic Liberal Party faction or neutral status.
subfiles.summary: Groups named members under Yoshida, Ono, Yamazaki, Shidehara, Shukuto, neutral, and recently joined categories.

subfiles.title: Communist Party and Japanese Police
subfiles.from: U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Points to an intelligence summary on Communist relations with Japanese police.
subfiles.summary: Flags alleged infiltration, recruitment, intimidation, and claims of a government plan to create a police state.

subfiles.title: Japanese Publications on Sakhalin, South Kurils, Habomai, and Shikotan
subfiles.about: Transmits Japanese Foreign Ministry publications on territorial claims.
subfiles.summary: Forwards two publications reviewing Japan's historical claims to the named islands.

subfiles.title: Communist Situation in Hokkaido
subfiles.about: Transmits a Foreign Office official's observations after a Hokkaido lecture tour.
subfiles.summary: Reports weak communist activity relative to other Japanese regions, visible anti-communist sentiment, and strong interest in UNESCO. Listeners sought information about Soviet conditions and feared a Soviet occupation of Hokkaido during a war.

subfiles.title: Recent Information Concerning Hokkaido
subfiles.from: Japanese Foreign Office official; received from K. Ohno
subfiles.about: Records observations and audience questions from a lecture tour of Hokkaido.
subfiles.summary: The official describes anti-communist organizing, active UNESCO chapters, and estimates of Communist Party members and sympathizers. Audiences asked about Soviet life, U.S. withdrawal in a war, labor relations, China, Okinawa, and Taiwan.

subfiles.title: Letter Enclosing Monthly Reports
subfiles.from: Leonard Jaco II, International Telephone and Telegraph Corporation
subfiles.about: Sends excerpts from overseas subsidiaries' monthly reports.
subfiles.summary: Forwards political and business reports for State Department interest.

subfiles.title: July 1949 Report from Australia
subfiles.about: Describes the New South Wales coal strike and power restrictions.
subfiles.summary: Reports continued industrial power limits and federal use of the Army to operate open cut mines.

subfiles.title: June 1949 Report from Japan
subfiles.about: Reviews Japanese cabinet changes, trade agreements, ministry reorganization, and antimonopoly amendments.
subfiles.summary: The report notes Masuda's appointment and the division of the Communications Ministry. It outlines commercial arrangements with Argentina, the French Union, Peru, Finland, and Pakistan, then summarizes revisions to Japan's Anti-Monopoly Law affecting technology agreements, share ownership, debentures, and company officials.

subfiles.title: Article by Fuse Katsuji on Chances for a Bolshevik Revolution in Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits and summarizes Fuse's article on Soviet strategy and revolution in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The despatch recounts Fuse's interpretation of Lenin and Stalin, Soviet involvement in China, and a comparison between postwar Japan and Russia in 1917. It highlights Fuse's claim that Soviet strategy now treats Japan as an oppressed nation vulnerable to communist revolution.

subfiles.title: Chances for a Bolshevik Revolution of Japan
subfiles.about: Begins Fuse's account of Soviet revolutionary strategy in Asia and China.
subfiles.summary: Fuse recalls meetings with Lenin and Stalin and describes early Comintern efforts to train Asian revolutionaries. He traces Soviet cooperation with Sun Yat-sen and Chiang Kai-shek, the Northern Expedition, and Chiang's break with the Communists. The article continues beyond page 128.
